MESSI

Lionel Andrés Messi

A boy from Rosario who was told he was too small, signed his first contract on a paper napkin, and grew into the most decorated footballer in history. Eight Ballon d'Or awards. A World Cup. A left foot that changed the game.

History

From Rosario to the world

Scroll through the key moments of a career that spans four decades and three continents.

Rosario
1987

Born in Rosario

Lionel Andrés Messi is born on 24 June to Jorge, a steel-factory manager, and Celia, a part-time cleaner. He kicks his first ball in the streets of the Las Heras neighbourhood.

1992

First club, Grandoli

At five he joins local club Grandoli, coached by his father. His grandmother Celia takes him to training. He later points to the sky after goals in her memory.

1995

Newell's Old Boys

He joins Newell's youth teams. His side loses just one game in four years and becomes known as "The Machine of '87".

1997

Too small to play?

At ten he is diagnosed with a growth hormone deficiency. The treatment costs about $1,000 a month, more than his family can afford. Local clubs will not pay for it.

Barcelona
2000

The napkin contract

On 14 December, Barcelona director Carles Rexach writes an agreement on a paper napkin. The club offers to cover his treatment, and the family moves to Spain. Messi is 13.

2004

First-team debut

At 17 he debuts against Espanyol on 16 October. Months later, Ronaldinho sets up his first goal, a chip against Albacete.

2005

Youth world champion

He wins the FIFA U-20 World Cup with Argentina, finishing as top scorer and best player.

2008

Olympic gold

Barcelona initially refuse to release him. Pep Guardiola lets him go to Beijing, and he wins gold with Argentina.

2009

The sextuple and a first Ballon d'Or

Under Guardiola, Barcelona win six trophies in one year. Messi heads the winner in the Champions League final and takes his first Ballon d'Or.

2012

91 goals in a year

He breaks Gerd Müller's 40-year-old record for goals in a calendar year, finishing with 91 for club and country.

2014

So close in Brazil

He carries Argentina to the World Cup final at the Maracanã. Germany win 1–0 in extra time. He receives the Golden Ball, but the trophy he wants passes him by.

2015

MSN and a second treble

With Suárez and Neymar alongside him, Barcelona win La Liga, the Copa del Rey and the Champions League.

2016

Retirement, then return

After a third straight final defeat with Argentina, he announces his international retirement. Weeks later he changes his mind.

Glory
2021

Copa América, at last

Argentina beat Brazil 1–0 at the Maracanã. It is his first major senior title with his country. In August, a tearful goodbye to Barcelona, and a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

2022

World champion

In Qatar he scores twice in a 3–3 final against France, then converts in the shootout. Argentina win their third World Cup. He wins his second Golden Ball.

2023

Miami and an eighth Ballon d'Or

He joins Inter Miami and wins the Leagues Cup within weeks, the club's first trophy. In October he lifts his record eighth Ballon d'Or.

2024

Back-to-back Copas

Argentina retain the Copa América in the United States, beating Colombia 1–0 in extra time.

2026

A sixth World Cup

He becomes the first man to play in six World Cups. Argentina win their group, beat England in the semi-final, and fall to Spain in the final.

Replay

The Getafe goal

18 April 2007Copa del Rey semi-finalCamp Nou

Aged 19, Messi picks the ball up in his own half and runs past defender after defender, rounds the goalkeeper, and scores. Commentators compared it at once to Maradona's goal against England in 1986. Press play to watch the run.
